claims.text: Gear ratio is the number of teeth on the chainring divided by the number of teeth on the rear cog.
A higher gear ratio means the rear wheel turns more times for each full turn of the pedals, so it is a harder gear.
Development is the distance the bicycle travels for one full turn of the pedals.
Development equals the gear ratio multiplied by the circumference of the wheel.

says.wrong: A bigger ratio is an easier gear, because the pedals turn easily when the wheel is large.
says.wrong_again: No, I am fairly sure it is easier, since more teeth means more help from the chain.
says.right: The ratio is chainring teeth over cog teeth, and the higher it is the more the wheel turns per pedal turn, which makes it harder to pedal.

says.full: The ratio is chainring teeth divided by cog teeth, and a higher ratio is a harder gear because the wheel turns more for each pedal turn.

claims.text: The growth factor for one period is one plus the interest rate per period.
After n periods the balance is the starting amount multiplied by the growth factor raised to the power n.
Doubling time is the number of periods after which the balance is twice the starting amount.
The rule of 72 estimates the doubling time in years as 72 divided by the percentage rate.

says.right: The factor for one period is one plus the rate, and after n periods you multiply the start by that factor n times, so it is the factor to the power n.

claims.text: Binary search compares the target with the middle item of a sorted list and discards the half that cannot hold it.
Each comparison halves the number of items still in play.
The number of comparisons is about log base 2 of the list length, rounded up.
Binary search needs the list to be sorted, and on an unsorted list it can miss the target.
